purpose: Cross-check the production exact scalar dynamic program against direct deterministic public-history policy-table enumeration over the same declared one-step kernel.
claim_level: algorithmically distinct paths with a shared declared one-step kernel

shared_dependencies.role: Constructs the exact declared one-step transition kernel. This is a shared semantic dependency, not an independent reimplementation.
Provides the production value under test. The direct enumerator functions may not call or import this recursion.

forbidden_reference_reuse: src/oracle.py mass-state recursion or memo table
src/producer.py certificate, coupling, tree, or Bellman synthesis
src/campaign.py or src/summarize.py derived scientific results
required_scientific_validation: successful is true and failures and errors are zero.
All required coverage counts match the declared grids.
The retained optimum sums and exact-value histograms match a fresh recomputation.
Every generated input is recomputed by direct policy enumeration and compared exactly with the production scalar result.
snapshot_policy: No source or result hash is promised. Removing the stale fingerprint fields cancels only a snapshot-fingerprint claim; scientific validation is performed by required-field checks and fresh recomputation.
limitations: Algorithmic path diversity reduces common-code risk but is not proof-assistant verification or external replication.
Both paths depend on the same declared one-step kernel and may share a specification error.
Only scalar optima summaries and aggregate coverage are retained; no optimizing policy is stored.
